--- title: DATASCI 350 - Data Science Computing subtitle: "Lecture 25 - Docker for Data Science" author: - name: Danilo Freire email: danilo.freire@emory.edu affiliations: "Department of Data and Decision Sciences
Emory University" format: clean-revealjs: self-contained: false code-overflow: wrap footer: "[Docker](https://danilofreire.github.io/datasci350/lectures/lecture-25/25-docker.html)" transition: slide transition-speed: default scrollable: true engine: knitr lang: en-GB revealjs-plugins: - fontawesome - multimodal editor: render-on-save: true --- # Hello again! 😊 {background-color="#1B3A6B"} # Brief recap 📚 {background-color="#1B3A6B"} ## Dependencies, environments, and containers :::{style="margin-top: 40px; font-size: 21px;"} :::{.columns} :::{.column width="54%"} - We [pinned]{.alert} dependencies with `==` - [`venv`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/venv.html), [`pip`](https://pip.pypa.io/) and [`uv`](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) gave us an isolated Python - The project starter builds one at [`/opt/venv`]{.alert} - [Docker's three main concepts](https://docs.docker.com/learn/content/what-is-a-container/): - An [image]{.alert} is the recipe - A [container]{.alert} is a running instance - A [registry]{.alert} is where images live - A [six-instruction Dockerfile]{.alert} from `python:3.14-slim` built in 13 seconds - The cached rebuild took [less than 1 second]{.alert} - We pushed it to [`danilofreire/datasci350-example`](https://hub.docker.com/r/danilofreire/datasci350-example) on [Docker Hub](https://hub.docker.com/) - [Today we install Quarto in the image and render a report]{.alert} ::: :::{.column width="46%"} - What we did last time: :::{style="font-size: 20px;"} ```text docker build -t datasci350-example . #5 [1/5] FROM docker.io/library/python:3.14-slim #5 DONE 0.0s #6 [2/5] WORKDIR /app #6 CACHED #7 [3/5] COPY requirements.txt . #7 CACHED #8 [4/5] RUN pip install --no-cache-dir -r requirements.txt #8 CACHED #9 [5/5] COPY hello.py . #9 CACHED #10 exporting to image #10 DONE 0.1s ``` ::: - I built today's image before class, so it is already on my laptop ::: ::: ::: ## The Dockerfile from Lecture 23 :::{style="margin-top: 40px; font-size: 21px;"} :::{.columns} :::{.column width="58%"} :::{style="font-size: 23px;"} ```dockerfile # Start from an official Python image FROM python:3.14-slim # Create /app inside the image and move into it WORKDIR /app # Copy requirements.txt from your computer # into /app (the "."), then install it COPY requirements.txt . RUN pip install --no-cache-dir -r requirements.txt # Copy hello.py from your computer into /app COPY hello.py . # The command that runs when the container starts CMD ["python", "hello.py"] ``` ```text # Build an image called datasci350-example # from the files in this folder docker build -t datasci350-example . # Start a container from the image, and # delete the container when it exits docker run --rm datasci350-example ``` ::: ::: :::{.column width="42%"} - `FROM` picks the base image, here [Python 3.14 on a slim Debian Linux](https://hub.docker.com/_/python) - Base images live on [Docker Hub](https://hub.docker.com/), where you can search for one - `WORKDIR` creates `/app` and runs every later step inside it - `COPY` brings a file from your folder into the image - `RUN` executes a command while the image is built - `CMD` sets the command the container runs when it starts - `requirements.txt` is copied before `hello.py`, so editing the script does not reinstall the packages - Today's Dockerfile adds `ENV`, which sets a variable such as `PATH`, and `SHELL`, which picks the shell for `RUN` ::: ::: ::: # Today's agenda {background-color="#1B3A6B"} ## Lecture overview :::{style="margin-top: 40px; font-size: 24px;"} :::{.columns} :::{.column width="50%"} [1. The project starter]{.alert} - How I will grade your container - Why `data/raw/` is in the repository [2. The Dockerfile]{.alert} - What each line of the Dockerfile does - How long the first build takes [3. Run, change, rebuild]{.alert} - Use `-v` to get the report out - Why rebuilds take under a second ::: :::{.column width="50%"} [4. When something goes wrong]{.alert} - I break the project twice and fix it - Open a shell inside a container - Clean up old images [5. Beyond one Dockerfile]{.alert} - Ready-made images for Python and R - Share your image on Docker Hub ::: ::: ::: # The project starter {background-color="#1B3A6B"} ## How I will grade your container ### Test it yourself before you submit :::{style="margin-top: 40px; font-size: 22px;"} :::{.columns} :::{.column width="54%"} - [The commands I run:]{.alert} :::{style="margin-top: 20px; margin-bottom: 20px; font-size: 27px;"} ```text git clone fresh-test cd fresh-test docker build -t datasci350-project . docker run --rm \ -v "$(pwd)/output:/project/output" \ datasci350-project open output/report.html ``` ::: - I only have Docker installed, so your image must bring everything else - These commands are [30% of the project grade]{.alert} - Run them on your own repository first ::: :::{.column width="46%"} - The rubric (page 5 of [project-instructions.pdf](https://github.com/danilofreire/datasci350/blob/main/project/project-instructions.pdf)): :::{style="text-align: center; font-size: 19px; margin-top: 5px; margin-bottom: 5px;"} | Criterion | Weight | |:---|:---:| | Reproducibility: the container builds and the report renders from a clean `docker run` | 30% | | Analysis quality: the research question, the method, the interpretation | 30% | | Communication: clarity of the writing and the visualisations | 20% | | Code quality: organised, readable, no dead code | 10% | | Git workflow: meaningful commits from all members, sensible repository structure | 10% | ::: :::{style="background: rgba(230, 57, 70, 0.1); padding: 12px; border-radius: 10px; font-size: 19px; margin-top: 5px;"} Run the pull script once and commit `data/raw/`. If `report.qmd` calls the API itself, it fails whenever the API is down ::: ::: ::: ::: ## The starter repository :::{style="margin-top: 40px; font-size: 20px;"} :::{.columns} :::{.column width="50%"} - Clone it from [github.com/danilofreire/datasci350-project-starter](https://github.com/danilofreire/datasci350-project-starter): :::{style="font-size: 23px; margin-bottom: 20px;"} ```text datasci350-project-starter/ ├── Dockerfile ├── .dockerignore ├── requirements.txt ├── report.qmd ├── README.md ├── .gitignore ├── .gitattributes ├── data/ │ └── raw/ │ ├── life_expectancy.csv │ └── life_expectancy_raw.json └── scripts/ └── pull_data.py ``` ::: - Only `scripts/pull_data.py` calls the API. `report.qmd` reads the saved files in `data/raw/` ::: :::{.column width="50%"} :::{style="text-align: center; font-size: 17px; margin-top: 0px; margin-bottom: 10px;"} | Path | What it does | |---|---| | `scripts/pull_data.py` | Calls the World Bank API once and saves the response | | `data/raw/` | The saved snapshot, committed on purpose | | `report.qmd` | The Quarto report, with headings that follow the rubric | | `requirements.txt` | The pinned Python packages | | `Dockerfile` | The instructions that build the image | | `.dockerignore` | What stays out of the image | | `.gitattributes` | Keeps Linux line endings inside the container | ::: :::{style="text-align: center; margin-top: 10px;"} [![](figures/starter-repo-github-2026.png){width="58%"}](#){data-modal-type="image" data-modal-url="figures/starter-repo-github-2026.png"} ::: ::: ::: ::: ## The pull script and the saved data :::{style="margin-top: 40px; font-size: 24px;"} :::{.columns} :::{.column width="52%"} - Run the pull script once on your laptop. It downloads the data from the World Bank API: ```text python scripts/pull_data.py ``` - It saves two files in `data/raw/`: the raw JSON and a tidy CSV - The CSV has [96 rows]{.alert}: four countries, 2000 to 2023 ```text head -5 data/raw/life_expectancy.csv country_code,country,indicator,year,value BRA,Brazil,SP.DYN.LE00.IN,2000,69.584 BRA,Brazil,SP.DYN.LE00.IN,2001,69.98 BRA,Brazil,SP.DYN.LE00.IN,2002,70.396 BRA,Brazil,SP.DYN.LE00.IN,2003,70.884 ``` ::: :::{.column width="48%"} - Life expectancy is only an example. Change the indicator, countries and years at the top of `scripts/pull_data.py` - Commit both files, so the report uses the same data on every machine - The raw JSON lets you fix a tidying mistake without calling the API again :::{style="background: rgba(230, 57, 70, 0.1); padding: 15px; border-radius: 10px; font-size: 22px; margin-top: 20px;"} If you add `data/raw/` to `.gitignore`, the build still works. The report fails later, in my clone, because the CSV never reached GitHub: [[see it happen]{.button}](#sec-failure-one) ::: ::: ::: ::: ## `requirements.txt` for a report :::{style="margin-top: 40px; font-size: 20px;"} :::{.columns} :::{.column width="48%"} - The file, comments and all: :::{style="font-size: 20px;"} ```text # Talking to web APIs requests==2.32.5 # Data processing (use either, or both) # DuckDB runs SQL over your CSV files and # hands the answer back as a pandas # DataFrame when you call .df() on it. pandas==3.0.5 duckdb==1.5.5 # Plotting matplotlib==3.10.8 # Quarto needs these to run Python code # inside report.qmd ipykernel==7.2.0 jupyter-client==8.8.0 nbclient==0.10.4 nbformat==5.10.4 pyyaml==6.0.3 ``` ::: ::: :::{.column width="52%"} :::{style="text-align: center; font-size: 22px; margin-top: 0px; margin-bottom: 10px;"} | Package | What it does | |---|---| | `requests` | Calls the World Bank API | | `pandas` | Tidies the data and holds DuckDB's results | | `duckdb` | Runs SQL on the CSV, as in Lecture 22 | | `matplotlib` | Draws the figure | | `ipykernel` | Starts the Python kernel for Quarto | | `jupyter-client` | Sends your code to the kernel | | `nbclient`, `nbformat` | Run and save the notebook Quarto builds | | `pyyaml` | Quarto needs it to run Python code | ::: - Don't forget the last five! Quarto runs Python through [Jupyter]{.alert}, so the image needs a kernel - Nine pinned lines produce [53 installed packages]{.alert} inside the image ::: ::: ::: ## What `report.qmd` needs to render :::{style="margin-top: 40px; font-size: 20px;"} :::{.columns} :::{.column width="52%"} :::{style="font-size: 19px;"} ```python import duckdb import matplotlib.pyplot as plt data = duckdb.sql( "SELECT country, year, value " "FROM 'data/raw/life_expectancy.csv' " "ORDER BY country, year" ).df() print(f"Loaded {len(data)} rows covering " f"{data['country'].nunique()} countries.") fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7, 4)) for country, subset in data.groupby("country"): ax.plot(subset["year"], subset["value"]) [...] plt.show() ``` ::: :::{style="text-align: center; margin-top: 5px;"} [![](figures/starter-report-rendered-2026.png){width="40%"}](#){data-modal-type="image" data-modal-url="figures/starter-report-rendered-2026.png"} ::: :::{style="font-size: 17px; text-align: center;"} `output/report.html` ::: ::: :::{.column width="48%"} - [Three things]{.alert} the image has to provide: - A Python that has `duckdb`, `pandas` and `matplotlib`, and a kernel Quarto can start - The `quarto` binary itself - The file `data/raw/life_expectancy.csv` at that exact relative path - `embed-resources: true` puts the figures inside the HTML - `output/report.html` is [the single file your container must produce, and the one I grade]{.alert} - Rendered inside the container, that print statement says `Loaded 96 rows covering 4 countries.` - The header sets [`echo: true`]{.alert}, which shows your code in the report - The rubric asks for visible code, so leave that setting alone ::: ::: ::: # The Dockerfile 🐳 {background-color="#1B3A6B"} ## The whole `Dockerfile` {#sec-whole-dockerfile} :::{style="margin-top: 40px; font-size: 20px;"} :::{.columns} :::{.column width="56%"} :::{style="font-size: 20px;"} ```dockerfile # 1. Base image FROM ubuntu:24.04 # 2. Environment and shell ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive SHELL ["/bin/bash", "-c"] # 3. System packages RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y [...] # 4. Quarto RUN ARCH=$(dpkg --print-architecture) && [...] # 5. Python environment RUN python3 -m venv /opt/venv ENV PATH="/opt/venv/bin:$PATH" COPY requirements.txt /project/requirements.txt RUN pip install --no-cache-dir -r /project/requirements.txt # 6. Project files WORKDIR /project COPY . /project # 7. Default command ENV QUARTO_PYTHON=/opt/venv/bin/python CMD ["bash", "-c", "quarto render report.qmd && [...]"] ``` ::: ::: :::{.column width="44%"} - [13 instructions]{.alert} in seven blocks - The build log numbers eight of them, `[1/8]` to `[8/8]` - `ENV`, `SHELL` and `CMD` only record settings, so they get no number - The real file has a comment above every line. Read them before you change anything - Lecture 23's file ran one script. This one installs Ubuntu packages, Quarto and a Python environment :::{style="text-align: center; margin-top: 12px;"} [[Full listing]{.button}](#sec-appendix-03) ::: ::: ::: ::: ## Blocks 1 and 2: `FROM`, `ENV`, `SHELL` :::{style="margin-top: 40px; font-size: 20px;"} :::{.columns} :::{.column width="52%"} :::{style="font-size: 20px;"} ```dockerfile # We pin the tag to "24.04" rather than "latest". # "latest" changes over time, and a base image # that changes breaks reproducibility. FROM ubuntu:24.04 # DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive stops apt-get # from asking questions during the build. # Nobody is at the keyboard to answer them. ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive # Use bash for the RUN steps below. Docker uses # the simpler "sh" shell by default. SHELL ["/bin/bash", "-c"] ``` ::: - `ubuntu:latest` meant 24.04 last year and means [26.04]{.alert} today, so we pin the tag - `tzdata` is the Ubuntu package that would otherwise stop and ask you for a time zone - `ubuntu:24.04` is a [29MB]{.alert} download, 108MB once unpacked ::: :::{.column width="48%"} :::{style="text-align: center; margin-top: -10px;"} [![](figures/docker-hub-ubuntu-2026.png){width="46%"}](#){data-modal-type="image" data-modal-url="figures/docker-hub-ubuntu-2026.png"} ::: :::{style="font-size: 17px; text-align: center;"} [hub.docker.com/_/ubuntu](https://hub.docker.com/_/ubuntu) ::: - `ENV` also applies when the container runs - `SHELL` makes every later `RUN` use `bash`, and `-c` passes it a string of commands - The `ubuntu` image has no Python, so block 3 installs it - Quarto ships as a `.deb` file, which needs a Debian-based system like Ubuntu ::: ::: ::: ## Block 3: `RUN apt-get install` :::{style="margin-top: 40px; font-size: 20px;"} :::{.columns} :::{.column width="52%"} :::{style="font-size: 20px;"} ```dockerfile RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \ ca-certificates \ wget \ git \ python3.12 \ python3.12-venv \ python3-pip && \ apt-get clean && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/* ``` ::: - One `RUN` is one [layer]{.alert} - Six `RUN` lines here would give six layers and a bigger image - Clean up [in the same `RUN`]{.alert}: a later layer cannot shrink an earlier one - `--no-install-recommends` skips optional extras - This step took [less than a minute]{.alert} ::: :::{.column width="48%"} :::{style="text-align: center; font-size: 22px; margin-top: 0px; margin-bottom: 50px;"} | Package | Why | |---|---| | `ca-certificates` | HTTPS downloads fail without it | | `wget` | Fetches the Quarto `.deb` | | `git` | Some Quarto extensions want it | | `python3.12` | The interpreter, version 3.12.3 here | | `python3.12-venv` | Ubuntu ships `venv` separately | | `python3-pip` | Installs into the virtual environment | ::: ::: ::: ::: ## Block 4: Quarto :::{style="margin-top: 40px; font-size: 20px;"} :::{.columns} :::{.column width="54%"} :::{style="font-size: 20px;"} ```dockerfile RUN ARCH=$(dpkg --print-architecture) && \ wget -q "https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/releases/download/v1.10.18/quarto-1.10.18-linux-${ARCH}.deb" && \ apt-get update && \ apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends ./quarto-1.10.18-linux-${ARCH}.deb && \ rm quarto-1.10.18-linux-${ARCH}.deb && \ apt-get clean && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/* ``` ::: - Quarto is not in Ubuntu's package list, so we download the `.deb` from GitHub :::{style="font-size: 20px;"} ```text #7 91.74 Setting up quarto (1.10.18) ... #7 DONE 92.0s ``` ::: - [92 seconds]{.alert}, the slowest step in the build - `./` tells apt to install the downloaded file, not search its list - `apt-get update` runs again because block 3 deleted the package lists ::: :::{.column width="46%"} - The version [1.10.18]{.alert} is written out, so everyone builds the same image - It appears four times in this step. Change all four to update Quarto - `dpkg --print-architecture` gives `arm64` on a Mac and `amd64` on most Windows and Linux laptops, so each downloads the right file - My laptop has Quarto 1.9.38, but your report renders with the image's [1.10.18]{.alert} ::: ::: ::: ## Block 5: the virtual environment and `pip` {#sec-block-5} :::{style="margin-top: 40px; font-size: 20px;"} :::{.columns} :::{.column width="52%"} :::{style="font-size: 20px;"} ```dockerfile # Ubuntu protects its own Python installation, # so we create a virtual environment at # /opt/venv and install our packages there. RUN python3 -m venv /opt/venv # PATH tells the shell where to look for # programs. Putting /opt/venv/bin first means # "python" and "pip" refer to the virtual # environment, without activating it by hand. ENV PATH="/opt/venv/bin:$PATH" # We copy requirements.txt on its own, before # the rest of the project. COPY requirements.txt /project/requirements.txt RUN pip install --no-cache-dir -r /project/requirements.txt ``` ::: - [`ENV PATH`]{.alert} replaces Lecture 23's `source .venv/bin/activate` - Ubuntu blocks a system-wide `pip install` with [`externally-managed-environment`]{.alert}, so we use a virtual environment: [[Appendix 02]{.button}](#sec-appendix-02) ::: :::{.column width="48%"} - `COPY` puts your `requirements.txt` inside the image, and `pip` installs from that copy - `--no-cache-dir` keeps pip's downloads out of the image - The install took [less than a minute]{.alert} and produced 53 packages - `COPY requirements.txt` comes before `COPY . /project`, so editing `report.qmd` does not rerun this step ::: ::: ::: ## Blocks 6 and 7: `WORKDIR`, `COPY .`, `CMD` :::{style="margin-top: 40px; font-size: 20px;"} :::{.columns} :::{.column width="54%"} :::{style="font-size: 19px;"} ```dockerfile # WORKDIR sets the folder that later # instructions run inside. WORKDIR /project # Copy everything else from your repository into # the image, including report.qmd and the saved # data snapshot in data/raw/. # The .dockerignore file next to this one lists # what stays out. COPY . /project # QUARTO_PYTHON points Quarto at the virtual # environment's Python. ENV QUARTO_PYTHON=/opt/venv/bin/python CMD ["bash", "-c", "quarto render report.qmd && mkdir -p output && cp -a report.html output/ && echo 'Rendered report is in output/report.html'"] ``` ::: ::: :::{.column width="46%"} - `COPY . /project` copies the folder you build from, the `.` in `docker build` - The next slide shows what stays out - `QUARTO_PYTHON` tells Quarto which Python to use - The `CMD` joins [four commands]{.alert} with `&&`: render, create `output/`, copy the report there, print a message - Quarto renders in `/project` first, because it cannot clear a folder mounted from your laptop - The `CMD` list starts with `bash`, which gives us the shell that `&&` needs ::: ::: ::: ## `.dockerignore` :::{style="margin-top: 40px; font-size: 19px;"} :::{.columns} :::{.column width="50%"} :::{style="font-size: 19px;"} ```text # Version control .git # Python environments and caches .venv/ venv/ __pycache__/ # API keys never enter the image .env # Quarto working files and rendered output .quarto/ *.quarto_ipynb report.html report_files/ output/ # Operating system clutter .DS_Store # NOTE: data/raw/ is deliberately absent. The # snapshot must reach the image, because # report.qmd reads it. ``` ::: - Save it next to your `Dockerfile` and commit it ::: :::{.column width="50%"} - Before it builds, Docker sends your folder (the [build context]{.alert}) to the engine. The same folder, with and without the file: :::{style="font-size: 20px;"} ```text === WITHOUT .dockerignore === #3 load .dockerignore: 2B done #5 load build context: 1.42MB done === WITH .dockerignore === #3 load .dockerignore: 578B done #5 load build context: 59.36kB done ``` ::: - [1.42MB down to 59.36kB]{.alert}, with `.git` and the rendered report left out - `.gitignore` keeps files out of Git, and `.dockerignore` keeps them out of the image - [Never list `data/raw/` in either file]{.alert} - Without `report.html` in the list, every render breaks the cache on `COPY . /project` ::: ::: ::: ## The first build :::{style="margin-top: 40px; font-size: 20px;"} :::{.columns} :::{.column width="54%"} :::{style="font-size: 18px;"} ```text time docker build --no-cache --progress=plain -t datasci350-project . #5 [1/8] FROM docker.io/library/ubuntu:24.04 #5 CACHED #6 [2/8] RUN apt-get update && apt-get install [...] #6 DONE 36.0s #7 [3/8] RUN ARCH=$(dpkg --print-architecture) [...] #7 91.74 Setting up quarto (1.10.18) ... #7 DONE 92.0s #8 [4/8] RUN python3 -m venv /opt/venv #8 DONE 1.3s #9 [5/8] COPY requirements.txt /project/requirements.txt #9 DONE 0.0s #10 [6/8] RUN pip install --no-cache-dir -r [...] #10 50.70 Successfully installed asttokens-3.0.2 [...] #10 DONE 51.4s #11 [7/8] WORKDIR /project #11 DONE 0.1s #12 [8/8] COPY . /project #12 DONE 0.1s #13 exporting to image #13 DONE 10.5s docker build [...] 3:11.77 total ``` ::: - `--progress=plain` prints the full log. Use it when a build fails ::: :::{.column width="46%"} - `--no-cache` runs every step again, which is how I timed it - The log has eight numbered steps, one per layer - Quarto ([92s]{.alert}), pip ([51s]{.alert}) and apt ([36s]{.alert}) take most of the time - `[1/8]` says `CACHED` because Ubuntu was already on my laptop. Its first download took 38.6 seconds - Total: [about 3 minutes]{.alert} :::{style="font-size: 18px;"} ```text docker images datasci350-project IMAGE DISK USAGE CONTENT SIZE datasci350-project:latest 1.52GB 347MB ``` ::: - An amd64 laptop downloads amd64 files and gets the same report ::: ::: ::: ## `docker history` shows the size of each layer :::{style="margin-top: 40px; font-size: 20px;"} :::{.columns} :::{.column width="54%"} :::{style="font-size: 20px;"} ```text docker history --format "{{.Size}}\t{{.CreatedBy}}" \ datasci350-project 0B CMD ["bash" "-c" "quarto render [...] 0B ENV QUARTO_PYTHON=/opt/venv/bin/python 81.9kB COPY . /project 0B WORKDIR /project 421MB RUN pip install --no-cache-dir -r [...] 4.1kB COPY requirements.txt [...] 0B ENV PATH=/opt/venv/bin:/usr/local/sbin:[...] 15.6MB RUN python3 -m venv /opt/venv 459MB RUN ARCH=$(dpkg --print-architecture) [...] 169MB RUN apt-get update && apt-get install [...] 0B SHELL [/bin/bash -c] 0B ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive 108MB ADD file:0387b3d029de8fa08[...] in / 0B [...] ``` ::: ::: :::{.column width="46%"} - `docker history` lists one row per [layer]{.alert}, newest at the top - [Quarto]{.alert} is the biggest layer at 459MB, ahead of pip's 421MB - apt adds 169MB, and the `ubuntu:24.04` base is only 108MB - `ENV`, `SHELL` and `CMD` only set metadata. `WORKDIR` gets a step number but adds 0B - A `CACHED` step skips the download as well as the work - `docker images` reports 1.52GB on disk and 347MB content, because content size is measured compressed ::: ::: ::: # Run, change, rebuild {background-color="#1B3A6B"} ## Running the container {#sec-run} :::{style="margin-top: 40px; font-size: 20px;"} :::{.columns} :::{.column width="54%"} :::{style="font-size: 20px;"} ```text time docker run --rm \ -v "$(pwd)/output:/project/output" \ datasci350-project Starting python3 kernel...Done Executing 'report.quarto_ipynb' Cell 1/1: 'fig-demo'...Done [...] Output created: report.html Rendered report is in output/report.html docker run [...] 3.237 total ls -la output -rw-r--r-- 1 dafreir staff 1314625 report.html ``` ::: - It takes three seconds, because the slow work happened during the build ::: :::{.column width="46%"} :::{style="text-align: center; font-size: 22px; margin-top: 0px; margin-bottom: 10px;"} | Part | What it does | |---|---| | `--rm` | Deletes the container when it exits | | `-v host:container` | Connects a folder on your machine to one inside the container | | `datasci350-project` | The image to start | ::: - [`-v`]{.alert} (volume): your laptop's folder goes left of the colon, the container's on the right - `$(pwd)` is your current folder. Use `${PWD}` in PowerShell or `%cd%` in the old Windows terminal - Recent Docker also accepts `-v ./output:...` - [`--rm`]{.alert} deletes the container as soon as it finishes - Only the report survives, because it was saved to the mounted folder ::: ::: ::: ## Forgetting the mount :::{style="margin-top: 40px; font-size: 20px;"} :::{.columns} :::{.column width="52%"} :::{style="font-size: 20px;"} ```text docker run --rm datasci350-project [...] Output created: report.html Rendered report is in output/report.html ls output ls: output: No such file or directory exit code: 1 ``` ::: - The render worked, but the report stayed inside the container - `--rm` then deleted the container, and the report with it ::: :::{.column width="48%"} - Listing `output/` inside the container shows the report was there: :::{style="font-size: 20px;"} ```text docker run --rm datasci350-project bash -c \ "quarto render report.qmd >/dev/null 2>&1 \ && mkdir -p output && cp report.html output/ \ && ls -la output" -rw-r--r-- 1 root root [...] report.html ``` ::: - `>/dev/null 2>&1` hides Quarto's messages, so only the file listing shows - This is the most common Docker mistake in the course, and Docker gives no warning :::{style="background: rgba(230, 57, 70, 0.1); padding: 15px; border-radius: 10px; font-size: 19px; margin-top: 15px;"} Without `-v`, the report is deleted with the container. After every run, check `ls output` and the file's timestamp ::: ::: ::: ::: ## Rebuilding after a one-line change {#sec-rebuild} :::{style="margin-top: 40px; font-size: 20px;"} :::{.columns} :::{.column width="52%"} - I changed the title in `report.qmd` and built again: :::{style="font-size: 20px;"} ```text time docker build --progress=plain -t datasci350-project . #4 transferring context: 4.95kB done #5 [1/8] FROM docker.io/library/ubuntu:24.04 #5 DONE 0.0s #6 [3/8] RUN ARCH=$(dpkg --print-architecture) [...] #6 CACHED #7 [2/8] RUN apt-get update && apt-get install [...] #7 CACHED #8 [5/8] COPY requirements.txt /project/requirements.txt #8 CACHED #9 [4/8] RUN python3 -m venv /opt/venv #9 CACHED #10 [6/8] RUN pip install --no-cache-dir -r [...] #10 CACHED #11 [7/8] WORKDIR /project #11 CACHED #12 [8/8] COPY . /project #12 DONE 0.0s docker build [...] 0.666 total ``` ::: ::: :::{.column width="48%"} - Seven steps cached and one rebuilt: [less than 1 second]{.alert}, against about 3 minutes cold - Only `report.qmd` changed, so only `COPY . /project` ran again - `pip install` stayed cached, because `requirements.txt` did not change - The `[n/8]` labels show the real order. The `#` numbers are just log IDs - Change `requirements.txt` instead, and the cache misses at `[5/8]`, so pip and every later step run again - Rebuild after every edit. It takes a second and keeps the image up to date :::{style="text-align: center; margin-top: 12px;"} [[Try it yourself]{.button}](#sec-exercise-01) ::: ::: ::: ::: # When something goes wrong ⚠️ {background-color="#1B3A6B"} ## Failure one: the data is not in the repository {#sec-failure-one} :::{style="margin-top: 40px; font-size: 20px;"} :::{.columns} :::{.column width="52%"} - I added `data/raw/` to `.gitignore`, committed, and cloned the repository into a new folder: :::{style="font-size: 20px;"} ```text ls data ls: data: No such file or directory git ls-files data/raw (nothing) docker build -t datasci350-project-nodata . #13 DONE 0.2s ``` ::: - [The build succeeded]{.alert}, because the Dockerfile never mentions the CSV - It fails only when you run it :::{style="background: rgba(230, 57, 70, 0.1); padding: 15px; border-radius: 10px; font-size: 19px; margin-top: 10px;"} Always test from a fresh clone. Your own folder still has the files you forgot to commit ::: ::: :::{.column width="48%"} - The run, with the traceback trimmed: :::{style="font-size: 19px;"} ```text docker run --rm -v "$(pwd)/output:/project/output" \ datasci350-project-nodata Starting python3 kernel...Done Executing 'report.quarto_ipynb' Cell 1/1: 'fig-demo'... An error occurred while executing the following cell: [...] data = duckdb.sql("SELECT country, year, value " "FROM 'data/raw/life_expectancy.csv' [...]").df() [...] IOException: IO Error: No files found that match the pattern "data/raw/life_expectancy.csv" WARN: Error encountered when rendering files exit code: 1 ``` ::: - Fix it with `git add data/raw/` and `git commit` - `git ls-files data/raw` should then print two file names ::: ::: ::: ## Failure two: a pin that does not exist :::{style="margin-top: 40px; font-size: 20px;"} :::{.columns} :::{.column width="54%"} - I changed `duckdb==1.5.5` to `duckdb==1.5.9` and built: :::{style="font-size: 19px;"} ```text #10 [6/8] RUN pip install --no-cache-dir -r [...] #10 0.818 Collecting pandas==3.0.5 [...] #10 1.302 ERROR: Could not find a version that satisfies the requirement duckdb==1.5.9 (from versions: [...] 1.5.4, 1.5.5, 1.5.6.dev36, 1.6.0.dev379, 2.0.0.dev2609121639) #10 1.302 ERROR: No matching distribution found for duckdb==1.5.9 Dockerfile:85 -------------------- 84 | COPY requirements.txt /project/requirements.txt 85 | >>> RUN pip install --no-cache-dir -r /project/requirements.txt -------------------- ERROR: failed to build: failed to solve: process "/bin/bash -c pip install [...]" did not complete successfully: exit code: 1 ``` ::: ::: :::{.column width="46%"} - The error tells you three things: - `[6/8]` is the step that failed - `Dockerfile:85` and the `>>>` marker point to the line - The message above them comes from pip - No image is created - Steps `[1/8]` to `[5/8]` stay cached, so the fix only reruns pip - Check that a version exists before you pin it: :::{style="font-size: 20px;"} ```text pip index versions duckdb duckdb (1.5.5) Available versions: 1.5.5, 1.5.4, 1.5.3, [...] INSTALLED: 1.5.5 LATEST: 1.5.5 ``` ::: ::: ::: ::: ## Inspecting a container that misbehaves :::{style="margin-top: 40px; font-size: 20px;"} :::{.columns} :::{.column width="52%"} - Anything after the image name replaces the `CMD`. Here, `bash` opens a shell instead of rendering: ```text docker run --rm -it datasci350-project bash ``` - Then look around as on any Linux machine: :::{style="font-size: 20px;"} ```text quarto --version 1.10.18 which python /opt/venv/bin/python python -c "import pandas, duckdb, matplotlib; \ print(pandas.__version__, duckdb.__version__, \ matplotlib.__version__)" 3.0.5 1.5.5 3.10.8 ls data/raw life_expectancy.csv life_expectancy_raw.json pwd /project whoami root ``` ::: ::: :::{.column width="48%"} - Check which Quarto, Python and packages you have, and whether the data is there - `-it` opens an [interactive session]{.alert}: `-i` keeps input open and `-t` gives you a terminal - `docker exec -it bash` opens a shell in a container that is already running - Anything you install inside is lost when you exit. Fix `requirements.txt` and rebuild instead - `docker logs ` shows the output of a container running in the background ::: ::: ::: ## Cleaning up :::{style="margin-top: 40px; font-size: 20px;"} :::{.columns} :::{.column width="52%"} ```text $ docker ps -a CONTAINER ID IMAGE STATUS 5594bb583fbd hello-world Exited (0) 2 hours ago $ docker system df TYPE TOTAL ACTIVE SIZE RECLAIMABLE Images 7 1 10.88GB 4.029GB (37%) Containers 1 0 0B 0B Build Cache 37 0 3.046GB 1.403GB $ docker rm 5594bb583fbd $ docker rmi datasci350-project-nodata [...] $ docker system prune [...] Total reclaimed space: 1.931GB $ docker system df Images 4 0 3.217GB 1.97GB (61%) Containers 0 0 0B 0B Build Cache 8 0 1.643GB 0B ``` - One project image takes [1.52GB]{.alert}. A few failed builds can reach 10GB - Docker never deletes images by itself ::: :::{.column width="48%"} :::{style="text-align: center; font-size: 17px; margin-top: 0px; margin-bottom: 10px;"} | Command | What it removes | |---|---| | `docker ps -a` | Nothing, it lists all containers | | `docker rm ` | One stopped container | | `docker rmi ` | One image | | `docker system df` | Nothing, it reports what is using space (`df` = disk free) | | `docker system prune` | Stopped containers, unused networks, dangling images, build cache | | `docker system prune -a` | All of the above plus [every image not in use]{.alert} | ::: - The ID comes from `docker ps -a`, and the first few characters are enough - A [dangling image]{.alert} has no tag. Rebuilding a tag leaves the old image behind - `docker run --rm` keeps old containers from piling up :::{style="background: rgba(230, 57, 70, 0.1); padding: 15px; border-radius: 10px; font-size: 19px; margin-top: 5px;"} `docker system prune -a` deletes every image no running container is using. Read the prompt before you type `y` ::: ::: ::: ::: # Beyond one Dockerfile {background-color="#1B3A6B"} ## Ready-made images :::{style="margin-top: 30px; font-size: 19px;"} :::{.columns} :::{.column width="52%"} - The [Jupyter Docker Stacks](https://jupyter-docker-stacks.readthedocs.io/) are official images with JupyterLab and Python packages, hosted on [Quay.io](https://quay.io/organization/jupyter) - `scipy-notebook` takes [5.28GB]{.alert} on disk - It includes NumPy, pandas, SciPy, scikit-learn and matplotlib - Start it and open the URL it prints, on port 8888: :::{style="font-size: 20px;"} ```text docker run --rm -p 8888:8888 \ quay.io/jupyter/scipy-notebook [...] Executing: jupyter lab Jupyter Server 2.20.0 is running at: http://localhost:8888/lab?token=d59aac5d7a7e... Serving notebooks from local directory: /home/jovyan ``` ::: - [rocker](https://rocker-project.org/) offers the same for R: `r-ver`, `rstudio`, `tidyverse`, `verse`, `geospatial` ::: :::{.column width="48%"} :::{style="text-align: center; margin-top: -10px;"} [![](figures/jupyter-docker-stacks-2026.png){width="40%"}](#){data-modal-type="image" data-modal-url="figures/jupyter-docker-stacks-2026.png"} ::: :::{style="font-size: 17px; text-align: center;"} Like our project, `scipy-notebook` starts `FROM` Ubuntu, with a few smaller Jupyter images in between. [Docs](https://jupyter-docker-stacks.readthedocs.io/en/latest/using/selecting.html) ::: :::{style="text-align: center; margin-top: 8px;"} [![](figures/rocker-images-2026.png){width="40%"}](#){data-modal-type="image" data-modal-url="figures/rocker-images-2026.png"} ::: :::{style="font-size: 17px; text-align: center;"} [rocker-project.org](https://rocker-project.org/images/) ::: ::: ::: :::{style="background: rgba(27, 58, 107, 0.08); padding: 12px; border-radius: 10px; font-size: 19px; margin-top: 0px; text-align: center;"} For the project, write your own Dockerfile. A 5GB image to read one CSV is far more than you need ::: ::: ## Where to put a built image :::{style="margin-top: 40px; font-size: 20px;"} :::{.columns} :::{.column width="52%"} - The [`buildx`](https://docs.docker.com/build/building/multi-platform/) command builds for both chip types and pushes the image: :::{style="font-size: 20px;"} ```text docker buildx build --platform linux/amd64,linux/arm64 \ -t danilofreire/datasci350-project:latest --push . [...] => => pushing manifest for docker.io/danilofreire/ datasci350-project:latest@sha256:3136ee8fff92... ``` ::: - Docker Hub keeps one image per chip: [334 MB for amd64, 331 MB for arm64]{.alert} - Anyone with Docker can then pull and run it, with no build - [You don't need to push for the project]{.alert}. I build your image from your repository - A pushed image also freezes today's Ubuntu package versions ::: :::{.column width="48%"} :::{style="text-align: center; margin-top: -10px;"} [![](figures/docker-hub-project-2026.png){width="90%"}](#){data-modal-type="image" data-modal-url="figures/docker-hub-project-2026.png"} ::: :::{style="font-size: 17px; text-align: center;"} [hub.docker.com/r/danilofreire/datasci350-project](https://hub.docker.com/r/danilofreire/datasci350-project) ::: ::: ::: ::: ## Try it yourself at home {#sec-exercise-01} :::{style="margin-top: 40px; font-size: 20px;"} :::{.columns} :::{.column width="54%"} Use your clone of the starter. Step 2 takes about a minute 1. Add `seaborn==0.13.2` under `duckdb==1.5.5` in `requirements.txt` 2. Run `docker build -t datasci350-project .` 3. Read the log. Note which steps say `CACHED` 4. In the demo chunk of `report.qmd`, add `import seaborn as sns` under `import duckdb` 5. Add `print(f"seaborn {sns.__version__}")` under the `Loaded` print 6. Build again, then run `docker run --rm -v "$(pwd)/output:/project/output" datasci350-project` 7. Open `output/report.html` and find the line `seaborn 0.13.2` :::{style="margin-top: 12px;"} Solution and captured output: [[Appendix 01]{.button}](#sec-appendix-01) ::: ::: :::{.column width="46%"} What to look for: - Steps `[1/8]` to `[4/8]` stay `CACHED` - The cache misses at `[5/8]`, because `requirements.txt` changed - Every later step rebuilds, so `pip install` runs again for [less than a minute]{.alert} - The second build reruns only `COPY . /project` and takes seconds - The image grows from [347MB to 348MB]{.alert}, and from 53 packages to 54 ::: ::: ::: # Summary {background-color="#1B3A6B"} ## What we learned today :::{style="margin-top: 40px; font-size: 20px;"} :::{.columns} :::{.column width="50%"} - The starter has a pull script, the saved data, the report and a `Dockerfile` - I grade your container with five commands from a fresh clone ([30%]{.alert} of the project) - The `Dockerfile` has seven blocks, from the base image to `CMD` - `.dockerignore` keeps `.git`, `output/` and `.env` out of the image - `COPY requirements.txt` comes before `COPY . /project`, so rebuilds take [less than 1 second]{.alert} ::: :::{.column width="50%"} - Without [`-v`]{.alert}, the report is deleted with the container - If `data/raw/` is not committed, the build works but the run fails - A pin that does not exist stops the build - `docker run -it ... bash` lets you look inside the container - `docker system prune` frees disk space - [Ready-made images]{.alert} help you explore, and [Docker Hub]{.alert} lets you share - The appendices have the exercise solution and common errors ::: ::: :::{style="background: rgba(27, 58, 107, 0.08); padding: 15px; border-radius: 10px; font-size: 20px; margin-top: 15px;"} If `git clone`, `docker build` and `docker run -v` work from a fresh folder and the report opens, the container part of your project is done ::: ::: ## Next class :::{style="margin-top: 40px; font-size: 21px;"} :::{.columns} :::{.column width="50%"} No class on [Thursday 26 November]{.alert} (Thanksgiving) [Lecture 26]{.alert} (1 December) is revision. Bring your repository and questions, and we will build containers together [Quiz 05]{.alert} (3 December) covers Lectures 21, 22, 23 and 25. [Assignment 10]{.alert} is due the same day The final project is due on [8 December]{.alert} ::: :::{.column width="50%"} Before then: 1. Clone your own repository into a new, empty folder 2. Run the five commands from the grading slide 3. Run `git ls-files data/raw`. It should print two file names 4. Run `git shortlog -sn`. Every group member should appear ::: ::: ::: # And that's all for today! 🎉 {background-color="#1B3A6B"} # Appendix 📚 {background-color="#1B3A6B"} ## Appendix 01: Exercise solution {#sec-appendix-01} :::{style="margin-top: 40px; font-size: 16px;"} :::{.columns} :::{.column width="50%"} [Step 1]{.alert}, in `requirements.txt`: ```text # Data processing (use either, or both) pandas==3.0.5 duckdb==1.5.5 seaborn==0.13.2 ``` [Steps 4 and 5]{.alert}, in the demo chunk of `report.qmd`: ```python import duckdb import seaborn as sns import matplotlib.pyplot as plt data = duckdb.sql( "SELECT country, year, value " "FROM 'data/raw/life_expectancy.csv' " "ORDER BY country, year" ).df() print(f"Loaded {len(data)} rows covering " f"{data['country'].nunique()} countries.") print(f"seaborn {sns.__version__}") ``` [Step 7]{.alert}, in the rendered report: ```text grep -o "seaborn 0.13.2" output/report.html seaborn 0.13.2 ``` - Undo both edits and rebuild: everything is `CACHED` (2 seconds), back to 347MB and 53 packages ::: :::{.column width="50%"} [Steps 2 and 3]{.alert}, the rebuild: ```text #5 [1/8] FROM docker.io/library/ubuntu:24.04 #5 DONE 0.0s #6 [3/8] RUN ARCH=$(dpkg --print-architecture) [...] #6 CACHED #7 [2/8] RUN apt-get update && apt-get install [...] #7 CACHED #8 [4/8] RUN python3 -m venv /opt/venv #8 CACHED #9 [5/8] COPY requirements.txt /project/requirements.txt #9 DONE 0.0s #10 [6/8] RUN pip install --no-cache-dir -r [...] #10 18.77 Downloading seaborn-0.13.2-[...].whl (294 kB) #10 49.45 Successfully installed [...] seaborn-0.13.2 [...] #10 DONE 50.0s #11 [7/8] WORKDIR /project #11 DONE 0.1s #12 [8/8] COPY . /project #12 DONE 0.1s docker build [...] 57.726 total ``` - Four steps cached and four rebuilt, starting at `[5/8]` - pip reinstalled all 54 packages, not just seaborn :::{style="margin-top: 0px;"} [[Back to the exercise]{.button}](#sec-exercise-01) ::: ::: ::: ::: ## Appendix 02: When something goes wrong {#sec-appendix-02} :::{style="margin-top: 40px; font-size: 18px;"} :::{.columns} :::{.column width="50%"} [`IOException: No files found that match [...] life_expectancy.csv`]{.alert} `data/raw/` was never committed. Run `git add data/raw/` and commit, then check with `git ls-files data/raw`. [`No matching distribution found for duckdb==1.5.9`]{.alert} That version does not exist. Pin one that `pip index versions duckdb` lists. [`ls: output: No such file or directory`]{.alert} You forgot `-v`. Add `-v "$(pwd)/output:/project/output"` (`${PWD}` in PowerShell). Linux prints `ls: cannot access 'output'`. [`error: externally-managed-environment`]{.alert} You ran `pip install` on Ubuntu's own Python. Use a virtual environment, as in block 5. ::: :::{.column width="50%"} [`failed to read dockerfile: open Dockerfile`]{.alert} You are in the wrong folder. `cd` into the folder that has the `Dockerfile`. [`NoSuchKernel: No such kernel named python3`]{.alert} `ipykernel` is missing from `requirements.txt`. Add `ipykernel==7.2.0` back and rebuild. [`toomanyrequests: pull rate limit`]{.alert} Docker Hub allows 100 pulls every six hours without an account, 200 with one. Run `docker login` and build again :::{style="margin-top: 12px;"} [[Back to block 5]{.button}](#sec-block-5) ::: ::: ::: ::: ## Appendix 03: The complete Dockerfile {#sec-appendix-03} :::{style="margin-top: 30px; font-size: 16px;"} :::{.columns} :::{.column width="50%"} ```dockerfile # 1. Base image # FROM chooses the starting point: Ubuntu 24.04, # the system you saw in the containers lecture. # We pin the tag to "24.04" rather than "latest". FROM ubuntu:24.04 # 2. Environment and shell ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive SHELL ["/bin/bash", "-c"] # 3. System packages # We do not pin apt versions here. Ubuntu replaces # a version whenever it ships a security fix, and a # pin that no longer exists stops the build. The # base image tag and requirements.txt carry the pins. RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \ ca-certificates \ wget \ git \ python3.12 \ python3.12-venv \ python3-pip && \ apt-get clean && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/* # 4. Quarto # Quarto is not in the Ubuntu package list, so we # download the .deb from GitHub. The version is # written out in full, so the image you build is # the image everyone else builds. RUN ARCH=$(dpkg --print-architecture) && \ wget -q "https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/releases/download/v1.10.18/quarto-1.10.18-linux-${ARCH}.deb" && \ apt-get update && \ apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends ./quarto-1.10.18-linux-${ARCH}.deb && \ rm quarto-1.10.18-linux-${ARCH}.deb && \ apt-get clean && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/* ``` - Starter commit `cb64771`, with comments trimmed. Your clone has them all ::: :::{.column width="50%"} ```dockerfile # 5. Python environment # Ubuntu protects its own Python installation, so # we create a virtual environment at /opt/venv and # install our packages there. RUN python3 -m venv /opt/venv # PATH tells the shell where to look for programs. ENV PATH="/opt/venv/bin:$PATH" # We copy requirements.txt on its own, before the # rest of the project. Docker caches each layer. COPY requirements.txt /project/requirements.txt RUN pip install --no-cache-dir -r /project/requirements.txt # 6. Project files # WORKDIR sets the folder that later instructions # run inside. WORKDIR /project # Copy everything else from your repository into # the image, including report.qmd and the saved # data snapshot in data/raw/. # The .dockerignore file next to this one lists # what stays out. COPY . /project # 7. Default command # We render first and copy afterwards. Quarto # clears its output folder before writing, and it # cannot clear a folder Docker mounted from outside. # QUARTO_PYTHON points Quarto at the venv's Python. ENV QUARTO_PYTHON=/opt/venv/bin/python CMD ["bash", "-c", "quarto render report.qmd && mkdir -p output && cp -a report.html output/ && echo 'Rendered report is in output/report.html'"] ``` :::{style="margin-top: 0px;"} [[Back to the whole Dockerfile]{.button}](#sec-whole-dockerfile) ::: ::: ::: ::: ## Appendix 04: Docker Compose {#sec-appendix-04} :::{style="margin-top: 40px; font-size: 20px;"} :::{.columns} :::{.column width="50%"} - Compose saves the long `docker run` command in a file: :::{style="font-size: 20px;"} ```yaml services: report: build: . image: datasci350-project volumes: - ./output:/project/output ``` ::: - Save it as [`compose.yaml`]{.alert} next to your `Dockerfile` (`docker-compose.yml` also works): ```text docker compose up --build docker compose down ``` - Compose handles the relative path `./output`, so you don't need `$(pwd)` - Compose is mainly for [several containers]{.alert} working together, such as a database and an API ::: :::{.column width="50%"} - `down` removes the container and the network it created - Use `docker compose` (with a space). `docker-compose` (with a hyphen) is the old command - I ran this with [Compose v5.1.2]{.alert} - The starter has no compose file, so write your own - What it printed on my laptop: :::{style="font-size: 20px;"} ```text docker compose up --build [...] Image datasci350-project Built Network starter_default Created Container starter-report-1 Started report-1 | Rendered report is in output/report.html report-1 exited with code 0 docker compose down Container starter-report-1 Removed Network starter_default Removed ``` ::: :::{style="margin-top: 12px;"} [[Back to running the container]{.button}](#sec-run) ::: ::: ::: :::

<script>
  // htmlwidgets need to know to resize themselves when slides are shown/hidden.
  // Fire the "slideenter" event (handled by htmlwidgets.js) when the current
  // slide changes (different for each slide format).
  (function () {
    // dispatch for htmlwidgets
    function fireSlideEnter() {
      const event = window.document.createEvent("Event");
      event.initEvent("slideenter", true, true);
      window.document.dispatchEvent(event);
    }

    function fireSlideChanged(previousSlide, currentSlide) {
      fireSlideEnter();

      // dispatch for shiny
      if (window.jQuery) {
        if (previousSlide) {
          window.jQuery(previousSlide).trigger("hidden");
        }
        if (currentSlide) {
          window.jQuery(currentSlide).trigger("shown");
        }
      }
    }

    // hookup for slidy
    if (window.w3c_slidy) {
      window.w3c_slidy.add_observer(function (slide_num) {
        // slide_num starts at position 1
        fireSlideChanged(null, w3c_slidy.slides[slide_num - 1]);
      });
    }

  })();
</script>
